scheme1_name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)

comparisons.scheme1_value: Life Insurance — covers death due to ANY reason (natural or accidental)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Accident Insurance — covers ONLY accidental death and disability

comparisons.scheme1_value: Rs. 2 lakh for death from any cause
comparisons.scheme2_value: Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death only

comparisons.scheme1_value: No disability benefit; death cover only
comparisons.scheme2_value: Yes — Rs. 2 lakh for total loss of both eyes/hands/feet; Rs. 1 lakh for loss of one eye/hand/foot

comparisons.scheme1_value: Cover stops at age 50; cannot renew after 50
comparisons.scheme2_value: Cover stops at age 70; can continue until 70

comparisons.scheme1_value: 30-day waiting period — natural death in first 30 days NOT covered (accidental death IS covered from day 1)
comparisons.scheme2_value: No waiting period mentioned; but only accidents covered

comparisons.scheme1_value: 1) Filled consent form; 2) Self-attested KYC (Aadhaar/Voter ID/MGNREGA/Driving Licence); 3) Active bank account with auto-debit consent; 4) Nominee details
comparisons.scheme2_value: 1) Filled PMSBY application form; 2) KYC proof (Aadhaar as primary); 3) Active bank account with auto-debit consent; 4) Nominee details

comparisons.scheme1_value: Download form from jansuraksha.gov.in, fill, sign, attach KYC copies, submit to bank/post office. Receive Acknowledgement Slip cum Certificate.
comparisons.scheme2_value: Visit bank branch or download form from jansuraksha.gov.in/Forms-PMSBY.aspx, fill, submit with documents. Receive Acknowledgement Slip cum Certificate.

comparisons.scheme1_value: Through bank's net banking or mobile banking (Insurance > Social Security Schemes)
comparisons.scheme2_value: Through bank's net banking or mobile banking; SMS-based enrolment where offered

comparisons.scheme1_value: Auto-debited annually; cover runs 1 June to 31 May
comparisons.scheme2_value: Auto-debited on or before 1 June each year; cover runs 1 June to 31 May

comparisons.scheme1_value: Can enrol through only ONE account; extra enrolments get capped at Rs. 2 lakh total and premium may be forfeited
comparisons.scheme2_value: If covered through more than one account, total cover is restricted to Rs. 2 lakh

comparisons.scheme1_value: If auto-debit fails due to low balance, cover lapses
comparisons.scheme2_value: If auto-debit fails (account closed or insufficient balance), cover terminates

comparisons.scheme1_value: Natural death in the first 30 days of enrolment
comparisons.scheme2_value: Natural death from illness or disease; only accidents covered

recommendation: **Think of it like this:** PMJJBY is like a general health policy that protects your family if you pass away from any reason—good if you want broad peace of mind. PMSBY is like a cheaper accident-only policy—good if your main worry is accidents and you want to save money. **Which should you choose?** • **Pick PMJJBY if:** You are 18–50 years old, want broad death coverage (any reason), and can afford Rs. 436/year. • **Pick PMSBY if:** You are 18–70 years old, mainly worry about accidents, want the cheapest option (Rs. 20/year), or are older (PMJJBY stops at 50). • **Best idea:** If you can afford both, take both. PMSBY covers accidents; PMJJBY covers everything else. Together, they give you maximum protection for less than Rs. 500/year. **Disclaimer:** This is AI-assisted guidance based on official scheme records.
